The Friday Note · Issue #10

The Great Bifurcation

July 1, 2026 · Chris O'Hara

This week: PMM is forking into two distinct career paths. The middle ground—competent execution of standard PMM tasks—is exactly where AI is most disruptive. Here's what that means for your career.

📖 Feature

PMM Is Forking Into Two Different Jobs

At Cannes this week, Forrester dropped a finding that should have gotten more attention: nine in ten agencies now use AI, but the way they're using it is undermining marketing effectiveness. The efficiency-creativity tradeoff is real—and it's reshaping what PMM means.

The pattern that emerges from the data is a bifurcation—PMM splitting into two distinct paths:

🔧 AI System Architects

Train models on positioning. Design agentic workflows. Build the orchestration layer that makes AI marketing actually work.

✨ Human Premium Specialists

Strategic judgment. Customer empathy from lived experience. Narrative craft. The things AI can't replicate.

The middle ground—competent execution of standard PMM tasks—is exactly where AI is most disruptive. If your job is "write the battlecard, update the deck, draft the email," you're competing with tools that do those things faster and cheaper.

The question isn't whether you use AI. It's whether you're building the systems that use AI, or delivering the irreplaceable human elements that AI can't touch. Pick a lane.

📊 The Evidence

Five Proof Points from the Past Month

90%
of agencies now use AI — but effectiveness is declining

1. Forrester's Cannes Research: Agencies are using AI for efficiency, but creative effectiveness is suffering. The tools work; the application doesn't.

2. Adobe's Agentic Partnerships: Adobe just announced autonomous content agents. The "design and publish" workflow is becoming a single API call.

3. Amazon Rufus Conversion Rates: AI shopping assistants are converting at 2-3x traditional search. The buyer journey is changing.

4. Klaviyo's Trust Research: 68% of consumers say AI-generated marketing feels "less authentic." The human premium is real and measurable.

5. The Outcome-Based Pricing Shift: HubSpot moved to $0.50/resolved conversation. When AI does the work, the pricing model has to change.

💡 Implications

What This Means for Your Career

If you're early-career: Learn to build. Prompt engineering, workflow automation, agent orchestration. These are the new table stakes.

If you're mid-career: Audit your work. What percentage is "production" vs. "strategy"? Shift the ratio toward judgment, relationships, and insight.

If you're a leader: Restructure your team around the bifurcation. You need both paths—but you need fewer people in the middle.

The uncomfortable truth: Most PMM job descriptions are still written for the pre-AI world. The jobs are changing faster than the postings.
